This is a technical debugging task — a standard coding/troubleshooting query with no harm-adjacent, distasteful, or adversarial content involved. So the relevant deciding factor is capability fit, not the harm-aversion preferences that distinguish the two models.

The task is essentially extraction/retrieval-flavored debugging: diagnose a specific error trace (`!_src.empty()` means `cv2.imread` returned `None`, likely a bad/missing image path) and give a precise fix. Avocet-235B scores a bit higher on Extraction & Retrieval (81.6 vs 78.5), which most closely maps to focused diagnostic work, while the two models are effectively tied on most public benchmarks.

The user's request to be concise ("без воды" — no fluff) also slightly favors Avocet: Lapwing's documented strong appetite is for open-ended, novel, generative work, which is the opposite of a terse, deterministic bug fix. Neither model's quality is actually affected by these preferences per the documentation, but on the capability margin that matters here, Avocet was the marginally better fit.
